subject: Confirming residency SLA carve-outs & transient processing windows
messages:
From: Legal - Acme Health <legal@acmehealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Data Protection - Acme Health <data-protection@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Residency confirmation + proposed temporary processing windows

Hannah,

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. Before we can approve Redwood for our HIPAA-adjacent workloads, legal needs explicit language about two items:

1) A firm commitment that customer traffic and persisted model inputs/outputs for Acme Health will be anchored to the EU region for normal operations.
2) A narrowly-scoped exception describing the circumstances, maximum duration, and auditability for "transient processing" that may occur outside the EU (e.g., US) — we understand bursts for cache warming or emergency failover are operationally necessary but need hard limits.

Can you provide:
- Draft DPA addendum language that names the failover/maintenance window limits and audit log retention for those events.
- The current subprocessor roster and which subprocessors (if any) would be involved during a transient processing event.
- Confirmation that KMS keys remain EU-bound and that any egress is logged with token-level tracing for our auditors.

Attached is a short questionnaire from our data protection team and a redline template we use for residency commitments. We are on a tight procurement timeline (PO expected by mid-February).

Appreciate a response this week so we can align legal + procurement.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Senior Counsel, Privacy
Acme Health

Attachments: residency-questionnaire-acme.pdf (survey), redline-template-acme.docx
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Legal - Acme Health <legal@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Jan 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Residency confirmation + proposed temporary processing windows

Rachel —

Thanks for the clear list. High level answers here; attaching our initial addendum draft (residency-addendum-v1.docx) and ops playbook excerpt for the transient window. See quick summary below and happy to jump on a 30-min call to walk through.

Summary: 
- Region anchoring: We can commit that customer data (input prompts, generated outputs persisted to storage, audit logs) will be served from and stored in the EU under normal operations.
- Transient processing carve-out: We can agree to a controlled, auditable exception limited to operational events (maintenance, incident-driven failover, and cache warm-ups). Proposed maximum duration: 72 continuous hours per incident, with a cumulative cap of 168 hours per rolling 365 days unless pre-approved in writing by Acme.
- Key management: Customer-managed KMS integration is supported; by default KMS keys used for Acme accounts will be hosted in EU regions. Any transient use of keys in another region will be logged and surfaced in audit bundles.
- Auditability: Every transient event will produce an incident bundle containing start/end timestamps, affected subsystems, list of subprocessors engaged, and token-level tracing for sampled requests. Retention for these bundles: 5 years (exportable).

Next steps proposed: 1) Internal ops confirm specific subprocessor involvement (Jonas / Marissa on this thread), 2) we iterate the addendum, 3) DocuSign execution.

Short call availability: Thu 1/22 09:30–11:00 or Mon 1/26 14:00–16:00 CET.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Enterprise Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: residency-addendum-v1.docx, ops-failover-playbook.pdf
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Jan 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: follow-up for Acme Health — subprocessor & ops limits

Team —

Looping you in to confirm the operational constraints I outlined to Acme. Legal asked for concrete names and a dependable SLA/redline for the transient processing carve-out. Specific asks below: 

1) Subprocessors: which partners/systems would see data in a transient event? We should enumerate (e.g., edge cache provider, monitoring vendor, control-plane logs). Provide CSV for attachment.
2) Technical limits: can we commit to 72-hour continuous and 168-hour annual cap? Any systems that might require longer (e.g., large-model sharding during long migrations)?
3) Auditing: what does the incident bundle look like (fields), and who owns generation? Is there automation to produce a token-level sample for auditors?

Please reply with short bullets and point me to any relevant runbook excerpts. Acme wants the addendum this week if possible.

— Hannah

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <legal@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Data Protection - Acme Health <data-protection@acmehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Jan 2026 16:38:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Residency confirmation + proposed temporary processing windows

On Thu, Jan 21, 2026 at 10:03 AM Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Summary:
> - Region anchoring: We can commit that customer data (input prompts, generated outputs persisted to storage, audit logs) will be served from and stored in the EU under normal operations.
> - Transient processing carve-out: We can agree to a controlled, auditable exception limited to operational events (maintenance, incident-driven failover, and cache warm-ups). Proposed maximum duration: 72 continuous hours per incident, with a cumulative cap of 168 hours per rolling 365 days unless pre-approved in writing by Acme.

Thanks Hannah — quick ops specifics to make the addendum concrete.

Bullets:
- Subprocessors likely to be involved during a transient event: edge-cache provider (FastEdge Inc.), metrics/observability (PulseOps), S3-compatible object store replication (ThirdCloud Storage). Full roster attached (subprocessor-roster-2026-01.csv).
- Constraints: 72-hour continuous window is feasible. For scheduled migrations that might exceed 72 hours, we will require a pre-approved maintenance window and notify Acme 5 business days in advance.
- Key management: we support customer-managed KMS (recommended). If Acme uses Redwood-managed keys, we will restrict key material to EU-origin except during tested failover drills — those events will be logged.
- Audit bundle: will include: event id, start/end timestamps, affected model/version, list of subprocessors, origin/destination regions, representative token-level traces (sampled), and a hash index for integrity verification. Generation owner: Site Reliability (Jonas) with a 48-hour SLA to produce the bundle post-incident.
- Retention: incident bundles stored for 5 years; raw token traces sampled and retained for 30 days (full bundles keep hashes & metadata longer as noted).

I attached updated addendum language where I've replaced the generic caps with the proposed numbers and added an ops notification clause. Please review and let me know if Acme wants alternate language on the sampling mechanics.

Marissa Cole
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Dedicated

Attachments: residency-addendum-v1.docx (redline v2 embedded), ops-failover-playbook.pdf, subprocessor-roster-2026-01.csv
From: Legal - Acme Health <legal@acmehealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Data Protection - Acme Health <data-protection@acmehealth.com>, Procurement - Acme Health <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jan 2026 15:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Residency confirmation + proposed temporary processing windows

Hannah / Marissa —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the clarifications. The proposed caps (72 hours per incident, 168 hours yearly) and the notification + pre-approval language for longer scheduled maintenance are acceptable to Acme legal, subject to two small edits:

1) Replace "sampled token-level traces" with "pseudonymized sampled traces" and confirm that raw request content will not be included in exported bundles to legal reviewers.
2) Add an SLA for incident-bundle delivery: 72 hours from incident closure (we can accept Jonas' 48-hour internal target, but need it written as 72 hours for contractability).

If Redwood can accept those two edits, please issue a final addendum for signature. Procurement will then route a PO and expect a DocuSign packet (link below) after countersign.

We appreciate the transparency — this helps expedite our procurement loop.

Next steps: Revised addendum (hannah/marissa) -> DocuSign -> PO.

Best regards,
Rachel Kim
Senior Counsel, Privacy
Acme Health
